key_insight: Multi-STG combines LLM-derived semantic context with graph-based spatiotemporal learning to improve urban traffic forecasting under adverse weather.
engineering_relevance: The framework offers a way to incorporate weather, local land use, and holidays into traffic prediction when rare-event observations are scarce.
method: Encode weather, points of interest, and holiday descriptions into LLM-derived semantic embeddings.
Dynamically weight heterogeneous inputs through multimodal attention.
Refine forecasts with a semantic-enhanced prediction head using gated residual calibration.
evidence_signal: Experiments on real-world private-car datasets from three cities report an average 11.82% MAE reduction relative to the strongest baseline, with stable performance under sparse and non-stationary conditions.
watch_item: The abstract does not specify adverse-weather event coverage or LLM inference costs, leaving rare-event generalization and deployment overhead uncertain.
paper_title: Beyond Sunny Skies: Using Large Language Models to Predict Urban Traffic in Adverse Weather
